card.title: Frog — Digestive, Circulatory and Respiratory Systems

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: The frog's digestive system runs from the mouth (with a sticky tongue) to the cloaca, with the liver, gall bladder, and pancreas aiding digestion. The 3-chambered heart (2 atria + 1 ventricle) provides a partially mixed blood flow; the spongy myocardium reduces mixing. Respiration uses three surfaces: lungs, moist skin (cutaneous), and the buccal cavity; tadpoles use gills.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
Heart: 2 atria (right + left) + 1 ventricle; valves: AV (atrioventricular) + conus valves
Working: atria contract → fill ventricle → ventricle contracts → blood to lungs + body
Respiration: buccal floor down (inhale) → nostrils close, mouth floor up (exhale to lungs); skin respiration

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: The frog heart is 3-chambered (2 atria + 1 ventricle), NOT 4-chambered like mammals.  ·  Blood is PARTIALLY MIXED in the frog ventricle (unlike the 4-chambered heart of birds and mammals where it is fully separated).

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: NEB expects a labelled frog heart diagram plus the working mechanism.  ·  The spongy myocardium (crista ventriculi) is a key exam point.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Heart: right atrium (body blood) + left atrium (lung blood) + single ventricle (mixed).  ·  Digestive: liver + gall bladder (bile) + pancreas (digestive enzymes).

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: The spongy myocardium (crista ventriculi) in the frog ventricle helps reduce mixing of oxygenated and deoxygenated blood.  ·  Frogs use THREE respiratory surfaces: lungs, moist skin (cutaneous), and the buccal cavity; tadpoles use gills.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Digestive: mouth → oesophagus → stomach → intestine → cloaca; liver + gall bladder + pancreas.  ·  Heart: 3-chambered (2 atria + 1 ventricle); blood partially mixed.  ·  Spongy myocardium (crista ventriculi) reduces blood mixing.  ·  Respiratory: lungs + skin (cutaneous) + buccal cavity; tadpole gills.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: The frog heart has a single ventricle with a spongy myocardium (crista ventriculi) that reduces blood mixing.  ·  Frogs can lose up to ~25% of their water through the skin; cutaneous respiration is most active in water and at night.

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: Digestive system: mouth (tongue) → buccal cavity → oesophagus → stomach → intestine (small + large) → rectum → cloaca; liver and gall bladder; pancreas; bile for fat digestion.  ·  Circulatory system: 3-chambered heart (2 atria + 1 ventricle) → double circulation; oxygenated + deoxygenated blood partially mixed in the ventricle; systemic + pulmonary circuits.  ·  Heart structure: right atrium (deoxygenated from body), left atrium (oxygenated from lungs/skin), single ventricle (partially mixed blood); ventricle has a spongy myocardium (crista ventriculi) that reduces mixing.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Respiratory surfaces (lungs, skin, buccal)  ·  Buccal pumping  ·  Cloaca

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Bile and fat emulsification  ·  Physiology: buccal floor lowers (inhale), rises (exhale); skin respiration significant.  ·  Cloaca: common exit for digestive, excretory, reproductive.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Bile emulsifies fat; no enzyme in bile.  ·  The cloaca is the common exit for digestive, excretory, and reproductive systems.  ·  Bile (from the liver, stored in the gall bladder) emulsifies fat in the small intestine; it is not a digestive enzyme.
